items.text: 文 | 阿至 9月11日中国算力大会·太空算力创新发展专题论坛现场， 「星测未来」正式宣布完成A+、A++两轮累计数亿元融资 ，北创投、华映资本、新尚资本、新鼎资本等多家知名产业及财务投资机构联合投资，老股东锡创投、厚天资本持续加持。 半年数亿，这个体量是星测未来过去5年5轮融资总额的3倍还多。 这一幕对比更像整个赛道的情绪缩影。 马斯克用AI+太空的逻辑把SpaceX估值的天花板捅破，甚至放话未来四五年内，AI可能占到公司价值的99%。在他的叙事里，SpaceX是一家以星舰为基础设施、以AI为核心价值的科技公司，而未来，AI推理和计算的主战场将在太空。太空算力一跃成为2026年全球硬科技最炙手可热的赛道，在一级市场价值千金。 在中国，这个叙事被快速吸收、放大。一批创业者涌入赛道，钱的流动此起彼伏。 星测未来身处浪潮，被重新发现。 这个源自清华大学“天格计划”的团队，创业之初就提出AI在轨和卫星智能化。但那是6年前，“太空算力”这个词甚至还没有开始流通。 回过头看，星测未来是国内最早前瞻性布局太空算力并打通商业闭环的企业，标准化批量交付规模与商业落地速度均为行业领先： 37张先进制程GPU在轨部署、39颗载荷稳定在轨运行，率先实现国内12nm、全球7nm先进制程GPU在轨应用，单个设备在轨稳定运行超过四年。 但这不是一个幸运儿站上风口的故事。用星测未来CEO仓基荣的话说，“几乎一直在打逆风局，今年才开始顺风局。” 这话的背景并不复杂，公司成立的2020年，商业航天第一轮融资高点已过，行业仍处路线探索与基建加速的阶段，应用市场需求尚未起量，疫情则进一步加剧了创业公司要面对的外部复杂性。 或许就是因为生于“寒冬”，团队习惯了蛰伏，专注研发和在轨验证，精打细算每一分钱。当很多太空算力玩家还在论证产品可靠性、排队上天的时候，星测未来已经走完算力载荷验证和商业化应用的第一阶段。 “太空算力不应是停留在PPT上的概念，而是已经落地的在轨生产力。市场上有各种故事和技术路线，如果没上过天都是纸上谈兵，最终要看到底有没有在轨，有没有市场买单。”从稳定在轨运行数量和工程经验来看，星测未来更早走出了行业概念阶段，也接住了那个6年前自己押注的未来。 但这个故事的核心不是融资金额和数据，而是 一个长期被低估的团队，如何抓住属于自己的机会，又如何为下一个十年下注。 入局：瞄准AI+航天，三位“三清博士”的非典型创业 星测未来的创业源点可以追溯到2016年。当时，还在清华大学读博的仓基荣和曹德志，同为“天格计划”的核心研发骨干。 这是一个由清华学生主导的深空科研项目，他们自研科学载荷，搭载卫星平台进入太空，主要目标是探测和定位宇宙中的伽马射线暴。通俗地说，就是在太空中监测到“宇宙放烟花”的那个短暂瞬间，然后迅速把这个消息“告诉”地面，再由地面望远镜联合观测，做进一步的科学研究。 这里有两个关键变量，一是载荷自主识别和判断的能力，二是要尽可能快地传输结论。 2018年10月，“天格计划”首颗载荷成功入轨，完成国际首颗微纳卫星伽马暴探测载荷的全流程在轨验证——这也是星测未来星上智能处理技术和工程能力积累的源头。 对仓基荣来说，这段经历让他形成了一个关键判断：卫星只有具备数据在轨自主处理、筛选和决策的能力，才能最大化发挥其应用的价值。 卫星需要智能化，而AI是核心驱动力。 2020年，博士毕业的仓基荣和曹德志一拍即合，创立星测未来；同年年底，清华博士潘兴宇加入。三位“三清博士”（指本硕博士都在清华大学就读）正式组建联合创始团队，在“AI+航天”的交叉领域开启技术和产业化探索。 以星载AI计算为核心，星测未来2021年正式推出公司首款天基计算智能载荷“星溪”。 团队有共识、方向也选对了，但在疫情期间，钱的问题没那么好解决。第一笔天使轮资金几乎都投进了研发，但第一款计算载荷需要等待发射验证，才能拿到真正的市场反馈。现金流最紧张的阶段，账上只剩下两三个月的钱。为了支撑公司运转，团队开始承接一些外部技术服务订单。 “（这些订单）规模不大，但让公司活了下来，也补上了商业化的第一课。”仓基荣并不避讳谈起这段艰难的经历，他反复强调的是另一面：团队从低谷往上走，该蛰伏就要蛰伏，先积累技术和工程能力，尊重市场，理解经营。 2022年2月，终于等来了发射验证的窗口，星测未来首款计算载荷搭载12nm芯片，成功实现在轨运行，一直工作至今。 公司第二笔融资也顺利到账，来自客户和市场的反馈，让团队信心进一步提升。 一个细节是，2022年之后，无论挑战多大，星测未来的核心团队没有一个人离职。 这一批来自清华的博士生，没有航天院所背景，站在航天和AI的交叉口，依靠科研能力、工程经验和快速迭代，在国内率先把商用先进制程芯片送上了天，走通了一条过去“不被看好”的路线。 “航天是一项系统性工程。星链成本为什么能降下来？就是因为大量使用商用现货（COTS）芯片，这中间肯定有很多试错，发现问题解决问题，重要的是迭代速度。”在我们沟通的3个小时里，仓基荣提了17次“迭代”——这更贴近互联网和具身智能的思维模式。他相信迭代效率能够转化为产品竞争力，组织形态则直接影响决策效率。 基于这一认知，除了组建核心研发队伍，星测未来也在持续吸纳AI、航天、互联网、自动驾驶甚至大基建领域的专业人才，搭建出一套业务导向、效率优先的运营管理体系。成为商业航天领域中为数不多拥有复合背景的非典型创业团队。 蛰伏：在太空里“打怪升级”，工程经验才是真正的壁垒 如果用一句话概括星测未来在技术路线上的方向选择，可以先说个结论： 跟马斯克一样。 太空算力当下最核心的矛盾在于：宇航级芯片天然可靠，但成本高、迭代慢、生态封闭；地面先进制程芯片性能强、生态成熟、每代性能提升一个量级，但无法直接在太空环境中工作。 星测未来选择的是后者：基于地面主流GPU生态，通过系统容错和空间防护设计解决可靠性问题，走低成本、高性能、快迭代、广兼容的路线。 在具体方案设计层面做“三重保障”： 第一层是结构屏蔽 ，通过加厚结构件，将累积辐射损伤降低至原来的千分之一以下； 第二层是系统容错 ，用ECC校验（一种内存纠错技术）、冗余备份、看门狗等方式应对单粒子翻转等瞬态错误； 第三层是主动规避 ，在载荷上集成小型辐射传感器，实时探测粒子威胁等级，根据威胁程度触发不同级别的自检、修复甚至断电保护。 其中第三层设计，是星测未来的独家能力，基于过往清华工物系的空间环境认知积累。 “原来大家结构屏蔽、三模冗余的理念差不多，但工程上做到是另一回事。我们多了一层空间环境感知，多一维物理信息。”仓基荣说。 通俗地理解这两条路线的差异，就是过去航天解决抗辐照的思路是“硬扛”，用特殊工艺芯片在物理层面去对抗辐射。 星测未来的思路是允许芯片出错，让系统足够聪明，能够自主纠错，快速识别、修复，不影响在轨任务的完成。 这套设计方案不是坐在实验室里想出来的，而是通过长期稳定在轨运行、持续沉淀下来的工程能力。 星测未来第一颗计算载荷在轨验证成功之后，市场需求随之而来，产品验证加速，真正的“打怪升级”才开始。 在500至630公里轨道上，团队曾遭遇过高能粒子打翻存储器件、硬盘无法识别的情况，最终通过重新上注软件恢复；也曾遇到过单粒子引起的电流异常、功能故障，通过断电重启、看门狗复位等方式实现分钟级任务恢复。 仓基荣提到，团队对空间辐射的真实认知，都是在出错时获得的，“不出现错误时，我们都怀疑做了这么多冗余设计是不是有必要。直到经历过问题，才发现之前的很多设计都有价值。” 从2022年率先实现国内12nm芯片在轨应用，到2024年全球首个7nm芯片上天， 一个反直觉的事实是：在星上智能处理这件事上，国内企业并不落后，甚至在全球范围内走得更靠前。 但在仓基荣看来，算力入轨不等于在轨能运行，在轨运行不等于真正产生价值。在实际的市场应用中，开机时间、任务量、单位时间处理像素数、Token吞吐量（TPS）等业务指标，比标称算力更重要——这也对应了星测未来公司价值观中的第一条：价值创造。 “星测未来是一家商业公司，科研创新和技术突破是手段不是目的，我们需要持续为员工、股东、行业和国家创造价值。”仓基荣说。 反映到商业行为上，星测未来不是一家卖硬件载荷的公司，做的不是“一锤子买卖”。卫星上天之后，交付团队会在用户一线处理数据、调算法、帮用户把服务跑起来。星测未来2023年就开始参与国家级遥感星座项目，并顺利完成交付，随后陆续与航天领域的“国家队”单位和头部商业星座运营商建立了稳定合作。 过去几年，星测未来实际上是站在卫星公司后面，通过软硬件一体的产品+服务，和行业用户共同挖掘卫星应用的价值。 如今，这套打法正在向更长的行业链条延伸： 计算载荷是起点，场景服务是切口，算力运营是终局。 与之相对应，星测未来的商业逻辑也分三层展开：第一层是算力载荷硬件配套，目前已具备批量交付和在轨部署能力；第二层是面向垂直行业的感算一体卫星应用服务，在应急、交通等领域已有落地案例；第三层是太空算力基础设施与Token化运营服务，这是更长期的布局方向。 星测未来业务增长三曲线 来自应用层面的市场反馈是最直接的。 在应急能源领域，星测未来服务国家电网，为电力红外卫星A星提供智能计算与算法加速平台，实现红外遥感数据在轨实时处理、火点自动识别与高精度定位。该载荷于2026年2月入轨投用，官方数据显示，其单景影像检测定位耗时小于100毫秒。 水运交通方面，星测未来与中交水规院合作，布局利用卫星遥感与在轨算力，监测航道拥堵态势，同时拓展重大工程监测、多维环境监测、全球AIS跟踪增强等场景。 重点行业应用落地后，星测未来又瞄准金融保险、能源监测、应急救灾三大核心场景，与相关头部单位达成深度战略合作；国际维度，与海南卫星数据与应用研究中心达成战略合作，共同打造以"国际智能遥感卫星星座、天地一体化跨境感算平台"为代表的太空计算公共科技产品，助力构建天基智能应用国际开放合作生态。 一组最新的数据是， 星测未来目前在手订单规模已超1亿元，公司商业化落地进程加速，2026年营收规模预计将实现翻倍增长。 在交付保障方面，公司目前已储备超100套待发射算力平台，最高可支撑10POPS算力，已形成覆盖“星上边缘智能”到“太空算力中心”的算力产品矩阵。 跃迁：以“扶摇计划”为核心，星测未来要做一家怎样的公司？ 过去6年，星测未来的发展布局可以用四个字概括，天数天算。 让天上的数据在天上算，这依赖三个前提：硬件足够可靠、在轨数据足够充分、软件生态逐步完善。三者齐备，大小模型才谈得上在轨部署与协同调度，太空算力中心也才有从概念走向工程的可能。 沿着“实测—验证—规模化”的路径，星测未来已跑通天数天算的技术体系与商业闭环，同步正在布局太空算力集群的规模化组网与商用服务。在此基础上，推进从天数天算，向地数天算的演进，两条路径协同发展，最终搭建天地一体的算力架构。 在仓基荣的规划里，星测未来在为太空算力提供基础设施的同时，也要持续向下游走，深入各行业市场的一线，直接为终端用户提供Token化的运营服务。 在这套框架里，Token是数据、算力、模型、网络四项要素能力的结合。 星测未来战略布局 定位变化背后的思考逻辑是：商业航天要加速闭环，下游应用是关键。而星测未来站在AI与航天交叉点上，角色和身段更灵活，有望促进行业生态的整合与应用闭环。 今天星测未来正式官宣的“扶摇计划”，就以加速推进上述目标实现为核心。 扶摇星座采用“自建核心+生态共建”的差异化发展路径 ，整体规划303颗自研核心算力卫星，包含3颗1000P级旗舰型中心算力星、60颗10P级增强型节点算力星、240颗P级基础型边缘感算星三个梯度，形成全覆盖、分层级的在轨算力供给体系。再联动约3000颗行业生态共建卫星，打造分布式、高弹性、可拓展的太空智能算力集群。 星测未来“扶摇计划” 区别于单一组网路径，共建模式是这个计划中值得关注的部分。 过去，星测未来是卫星公司的供应商，赚载荷订单的钱。现在它选择主动让渡一部分硬件收入，成为星座共建方，直接面向下游行业应用客户，与卫星公司甲乙方关系互换，在数据与运营上深度协同，并按约定分润，这正是星测未来从上游部组件配套往下游应用服务转型升级的关键一步。 从经济账来看，这一模式不仅能够分摊硬件成本、加速算力星座组网进程。更重要的是， 它把过去分散在卫星制造、数据供应和应用开发三个环节的相关方绑定在了一起——用运营服务兑现长期价值，大家一起做增量，而不是分存量的蛋糕。 “行业整体的成本下降需要一个过程。我们希望通过共建共享模式降低行业组网门槛、提升太空资源利用率，加速太空算力产业生态普及。”仓基荣说。 目前，星测未来已与谱星航天达成生态合作，双方将联合打造1024颗智能遥感卫星集群，同时 面向全行业开放适配2000余套轻量化在轨计算载荷。 按规划，“扶摇计划”将稳步推进阶段性里程碑：2027年，完成2P级基础型、10P级增强型感算一体卫星技术验证；2028年，建成百星规模、百P级太空算力集群，实现全球覆盖、分钟级响应；2032年，完成303颗自建核心算力卫星全部入轨，构建自主可控的太空算力基础设施；2035年，完成共建星座全部组网，建成千P级全域分布式太空算力生态网络，实现全面Token化运营服务 。 在应用侧，星测未来计划打造“星海·太空物理模型”，把遥感监测、空间态势与辐照实测数据纳入统一的训练与推理框架，用于全球实时感知、态势推演以及卫星自主管控和星座调度。在其之上，行业定制小模型解决具体场景的精度与轻量化适配，AI Agent则把模型能力封装成可调用的任务流，按需调度大小模型完成一次作业。 大小模型+Agent协同的直接结果是数据处理位置的前移。过去卫星影像需先下传地面站、排队处理，一个流程往往以天计；在轨完成初筛与识别后，可剔除90%以上的无效数据，处理时延由天级压缩至分秒级，用户拿到可用信息的时间也随之从数天缩短到分钟级甚至更短。 与之配套的是按量计费的Token服务：Token既是算力消耗的计量单位，也对应数据、算力、模型、网络等要素的组合调用，用户为实际使用的部分付费，而非为整套系统买单。 至此，星测未来的收入结构也将从一次性的载荷交付和项目制服务，转向为可规模复制的运营服务。模型能力、行业应用与商业变现之间，才真正形成一条互相对应的链路。 从上游硬件到下游应用，星测未来的角色和定位转变，不单是一次业务延伸，这套选择逻辑最终还是回到了公司价值观的第一条，价值创造——技术要有人用，用起来要产生真实的商业结果。 而价值创造的对象，也不只是用户，还包括行业上下游、合作伙伴甚至是竞争对手。 除了前述星座共建计划，星测未来近期还公布了几项产业合作进展：与雷科空天联合攻关芯片级/系统级抗辐照关键技术；与中科密位协同打造太空智能计算全链路方案；与光子芯力合力推进光电算力芯片在轨验证。 其中不乏些出乎意料的合作。但这的确是仓基荣在沟通中数次提及的主张： 以合作共赢替代内卷。 在他看来，太空算力是一个足够大的赛道，远未到需要彼此争夺存量的阶段，企业之间各自优势不同，联合起来才能把产业共同做大。 就如同开源促进创新，先把少数人的游戏，变成多数人的赛道。 这条路径已经被反复验证有效。但前提是，作为一家创业公司要在更大的生态里持续证明自己的不可替代性。 6年时间，星测未来回答了一个最重要的问题：太空算力这条路走得通。 接下来的问题是，谁能让算力更快、更可靠、更聪明、更便宜的在天上运转，尽可能服务足够多的用户。以及中国太空算力公司，如何在国际竞争中找到自己的身位。 星测未来依旧身处竞赛之中。但好在，它已经提前站上了起跑线。 投资机构观点 北创投： 北创投始终聚焦高精尖产业领域开展投资，重点布局契合首都功能定位的前沿科技赛道。星测未来是硬科技成果转化的典范项目，其自主研发的星载计算平台已成功搭载近四十颗载荷在轨运行，技术成熟度与商业闭环能力均处于行业领先水平。我们看好星测未来在商业航天从“发射卫星”向“应用卫星”转型过程中扮演的关键角色，北创投将持续发挥国有资本的产业赋能优势支持企业成长。 华映资本创始管理合伙人季薇： 商业航天是华映近年重点布局的战略方向之一，我们认为明年将是行业大规模发射和商业化应用的爆发之年。星测未来是国内星载AI边缘计算的头部标的，卡位卫星智能化刚需，属于太空算力产业链“卖铲子”的最先受益环节。团队脱胎于清华“天格计划”，近40颗载荷在轨稳定运行，最长超4年，工程化能力已充分验证；“星溪”系列算力从21TOPS迭代至10P+，体现了其软硬件一体化闭环能力；同时公司拥有着清晰的商业模式规划。我们期待星测未来在星座建设浪潮中成为太空算力基础设施的核心供应商以及运营服务商。 新尚资本： 无锡新尚资本是太湖新城集团旗产业股权投资核心平台。星测未来所从事的星上智能计算与新尚资本重点布局的赛道高度契合，其国产化算力平台和存算传一体化技术具有明确的国产替代价值。新尚资本很高兴能在本轮成为星测未来的新股东，助力企业在太空算力领域持续突破。 新鼎资本： 新鼎资本的投资风格是深耕产业链、重仓长期价值。在考察商业航天赛道的过程中，我们发现星测未来是少数同时兼具技术壁垒、产品成熟度和客户认可度的标的。公司从芯片筛选、载荷研制到星上智能应用的全栈能力，以及在遥感、通信、科学实验等多场景的商业化落地，让我们看到了清晰的增长路径。新鼎资本在本轮选择入局，期待陪伴星测未来从行业先行者走向赛道领航者。 江苏康华投资集团： 江苏康华投资集团历经二十余年发展，在产业投资和实业运营方面积累了深厚经验。近年来集团积极向科技创新领域拓展，重点关注具有产业落地能力和规模化前景的硬科技项目。星测未来将航天级边缘计算技术与实际应用场景深度融合，产品已服务于遥感观测、应急救灾、空间目标探测等重要领域，商业模式清晰、客户粘性强。康华集团本轮参与投资，正是看好星测未来在太空算力产业化进程中的巨大潜力。 匀升资本： 匀升投资聚焦高端制造、医疗健康和新材料等战略新兴产业。商业航天作为国家“十五五”规划重点发展的未来产业之一，我们高度关注其产业链中的核心环节。星测未来在星上智能计算领域建立了从底层芯片筛选到上层应用算法的全栈能力，技术路径清晰、工程化程度高、应用闭环强。匀升投资本轮投资星测未来，是我们在商业航天赛道的重要布局，期待企业为太空算力国产化贡献力量。 晨峰基石： 晨峰基石持续关注商业航天产业链中的高成长性机会，此前已在商业航天卫星、部组件等领域有过成功布局。星测未来让我们看到了卫星载荷智能化及太空算力运营服务升级的巨大空间——在星座建设加速的背景下，星上计算及应用能力将成为决定卫星应用价值的关键变量。公司团队来自清华“天格计划”，技术底蕴深厚，且已在短时间内完成了从科研到批产的跨越。晨峰基石很荣幸在本轮参与投资，期待与企业共同成长。 海南见月： 见月投资专注于发现和陪伴具有高成长潜力的科技创新企业。星测未来所在的天基智能赛道正处于爆发前夜，随着低轨星座建设的加速推进，星上实时数据处理能力的需求将呈指数级增长。公司核心产品“星溪”系列智能载荷已在轨稳定运行，从技术指标到工程可靠性都达到了国内外行业领先水平。见月基金很高兴在本轮成为星测未来的投资方，期待见证中国太空算力的崛起。 惠丰达创投合伙人潘正亮认为： 商业航天、太空算力是我们长期关注并持续看好的未来产业，尤其太空算力作为国家重要的信息基础设施战略方向，值得长期支持与持续投入。星测未来作为太空算力领域的头部企业，具备深厚的科研积累与工程化能力，已构建超百套太空算力资产，独立运营30+套，在轨稳定运行超四年，技术壁垒与运营经验行业领先。公司以“感算一体”为核心差异化，将遥感数据处理从地面搬到在轨，实现小时级数据到分秒级结果的时效跃升，有效解决了传统遥感“数据利用低、服务时效差、应用门槛高”三大痛点。我们看好星测未来持续扩大星座规模，完善Token化服务体系，成为太空算力时代的基础设施运营商。 君一资本创始合伙人吴贤军表示： 算力上天，感算一体，天地协同，空间广阔。君一资本长期看好太空算力这一战略赛道，更看好星测未来团队在星载计算与遥感智能处理领域的长期深耕。公司核心团队源自清华“天格计划”，兼具科研深度与航天工程化能力，是国内少有的能完成从芯片适配、单机研制到星座运营全链条闭环的团队。星测未来提出的“全球太空算力Token运营服务领航者”定位，精准切中了行业从数据售卖向算力服务转型的关键窗口期。我们相信公司能依托自研算力卫星星座，为能源、金融、应急等行业提供高时效、低成本的天基智能服务，打开广阔的太空算力运营市场。 厚天资本： 作为星测未来的老股东，厚天资本从Pre-A轮开始陪伴企业成长，一路见证了团队将清华实验室里的前沿技术转化为在轨运行的成熟产品。商业航天是厚天重点布局的赛道之一，而星载智能计算及应用则是我们眼中卫星产业升级的核心变量。星测未来在产品迭代速度、在轨验证经验和客户拓展方面持续超预期，厚天资本在本轮选择继续加注，坚定看好公司成为中国太空算力基础设施的领军者。 锡创投： 无锡作为国家集成电路、商业航天与物联网产业高地，始终关注空天信息与算力基础设施的融合创新。星测未来团队在太空算力芯片适配、星载计算平台研制方面具有深刻的技术理解与独到的工程经验，公司组建了集芯片、航天、通信、AI等行业人才的跨学科综合型团队，形成了从算力芯片到星座运营的全栈能力。我们相信随着国产卫星运载能力的跨越式发展与卫星系统的通用化、智能化，太空计算能力作为基础性战略能力将迎来前所未有的发展机遇。星测未来有望在这一浪潮中解决太空算力基础设施的基础性问题，推动国产自主可控太空算力生态的构建，为国家科技创新与产业升级提供坚实支撑。

items.title: IEA警告：伊朗战争拖累石油需求创疫情后最大降幅，警告未来数月恐进一步走弱
items.summary: 布伦特原油在触及110美元关口后急剧回落，国际能源署（IEA）同步发出警告： 伊朗战争持续拖累全球石油需求，今年需求降幅已创新冠疫情以来最大，且未来数月可能进一步萎缩。 据彭博报道，
items.text: 布伦特原油在触及110美元关口后急剧回落，国际能源署（IEA）同步发出警告： 伊朗战争持续拖累全球石油需求，今年需求降幅已创新冠疫情以来最大，且未来数月可能进一步萎缩。 据彭博报道， IEA在9月月度报告中将今年全球石油需求降幅预测上调至每日250万桶，较上月预测深化94万桶，为2020年新冠疫情冲击以来年均需求最大跌幅。 IEA不再预期霍尔木兹海峡今年会重新开放航运 ，同时警告称， 随着供应持续受限、商业库存缓冲迅速耗尽，"未来数月可能需要进一步压缩需求以弥合供需缺口"，2026年和2027年将是全球石油需求增长的“失落时期”。 受上述警告影响，布伦特原油期货从盘中逼近110美元的高位急速回落约3.5%，跌至103美元附近。尽管如此，油价本周仍录得7月以来最大单周涨幅，年内累计涨幅已逾70%。 供应缺口持续扩大，库存以创纪录速度下降 IEA在报告中将今年全球石油供应年均降幅预测下调至每日570万桶，较上月预测再降130万桶，并将供应恢复预期推迟至明年 。综合供需两端，今年全球石油供应缺口预计约为每日175万桶，高于上月报告中每日130万桶的预测。 IEA将此次危机定性为"创纪录的供应中断"。 报告数据显示，今年2月至8月间，全球石油库存以每日280万桶的速度加速下降。第四季度库存预计将继续下滑，而IEA此前曾预测同期库存将出现小幅回升。IEA 8月报告还曾预计市场将于今年底前恢复供应过剩，如今这一判断已被彻底推翻。 霍尔木兹危机冲击流通，战争对供应的打击超过需求端 IEA指出，此次战争对石油流通的冲击甚至大于对消费端的影响，这正是供应缺口持续扩大的核心原因。霍尔木兹海峡咽喉要道持续受阻，能源基础设施遭受攻击的范围从波斯湾延伸至俄乌战场。 据彭博报道，伊朗支持的胡塞武装声称击中了沙特阿拉伯东西输油管道——该管道连接红海出口终端，是绕开霍尔木兹海峡的关键替代通道。与此同时，胡塞武装向毗邻战略要地曼德海峡的沿海地区推进，逼近红海南端的莫卡港。沙特石油产量上月再度下滑，降至1990年以来最低水平。 RBC Capital Markets分析师Helima Croft在研报中写道：" 沙特与胡塞武装全面战争的重燃，可能成为触发我们高油价情景的催化剂。" 柴油短缺冲击全球，亚洲石化产业首当其冲 IEA警告，2026年石油需求所受冲击的规模，可与过去60年中四次最大能源危机相提并论，冲击最为集中的领域是柴油等中间馏分油，以及亚洲石化工厂的原料供应。 柴油短缺已在全球范围内引发连锁反应。美国柴油裂解价差目前约为每桶110美元，全美工业用柴油零售均价达到每加仑6美元的历史高位，加利福尼亚州部分加油站价格已突破每加仑9.99美元。 Capital Economics大宗商品分析师Hamad Hussain警告，库存耗尽叠加中国需求早期复苏迹象，令油价对中东供应的任何新一轮中断高度敏感。前高盛大宗商品业务负责人、现任Real Macro负责人Jeff Currie在接受CNBC采访时表示，中国买家正在积极入市竞购原油，"我实际上更看重中国重返市场这一因素"。 外交斡旋现曙光，市场密切关注海湾局势走向 在地缘紧张持续升温之际，外交层面出现一丝缓和迹象。据彭博报道，海湾合作委员会六国正考虑于下周与伊朗官员举行会谈，议题涉及霍尔木兹海峡通行问题。 UBS分析师Justinus Steinhorst在研报中指出："布伦特原油在胡塞武装与曼德海峡局势引发双重咽喉要道担忧的背景下维持105美元上方，10年期德国国债收益率升至2009年以来最高，10年期美债收益率也逼近5%关口。" 市场当前面临的核心矛盾在于： 战争对供应端的破坏远超需求端的自然调节速度，而IEA的最新警告表明，在供应恢复前景依然模糊的情况下，需求侧的被动压缩或将成为平衡市场的唯一出路。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

items.title: ClickFix attacks infecting PCs and Macs are going viral
items.summary: It wasn’t that long ago that ClickFix attacks were exotic. Now the technique has become mainstream as attackers reap its simplicity and effectiveness in
items.text: It wasn’t that long ago that ClickFix attacks were exotic. Now the technique has become mainstream as attackers reap its simplicity and effectiveness in infecting users of PCs and Macs alike. All that’s required is a compromised website—a painless enough task—a fake CAPTCHA overlay, and the inclusion of a single terminal command. So many visitors get suckered into pasting and running the command that just about every malware pusher has adopted the technique. Even Kremlin-backed hacking groups are joining in. “Reddit is becoming post after post after post of people getting their computer infected via ClickFix,” independent researcher Kevin Beaumont observed Thursday . “Legit websites everywhere [are] getting hacked to serve the fake captcha prompts.” How many of us make things worse More seasoned Internet users—a fair number who read this site—are quick to dismiss the attack. They typically blame the people who fall for the scams and marvel at their gullibility and lack of attention. The reality is that for more casual users, using computers and the Internet has become so difficult—think impossible-to-close interstitials, CAPTCHAs with an endless series of pictures to analyze, and constantly changing interfaces that bury the features they’re looking for—that they have grown desensitized to instructions that seem ridiculous and burdensome. ClickFix attackers are capitalizing on this fatigue. Typically, attacks begin with a simple CAPTCHA image, often masquerading as one from Cloudflare. After engaging with the box, the user sees a line of text, often obscured in a way to mask any malicious commands. Then the user is instructed to copy the text and paste it into the Windows Run, PowerShell, or macOS terminal and click Enter. The instructions come from websites people have used for years. The directions seem no more suspicious than things they’ve been required to do for a decade. Why would someone without a firm grasp of computer security have any reason to hesitate? For the people behind the attacks, ClickFix now makes their job much easier. Prior to ClickFix, they would have needed to install the malware (tracked as Lorem Ipsum, security firm BlueVoyant said recently) using resource-intensive infrastructure, including SEO-manipulated and malvertised download portals, Microsoft-trusted signing certificates, and continuously rotated domains for delivering Microsoft Installer packages. “The pivot to ClickFix in late May 2026 eliminates the code-signing requirement entirely, substituting the legitimacy of a validly signed installer with a different form of legitimacy: a user voluntarily executing the malicious command in their own terminal,” BlueVoyant said. “[T]he ClickFix model broadens the victim pool from users searching specifically for Microsoft Teams to anyone browsing a compromised website.” The situation for macOS users isn’t any better. Both Mac security firm Jamf and a researcher have ​​documented macOS variations of ClickFix that can bypass Gatekeeper protections. ClickFix attackers keep finding new ways to use public services—including publicly published Google Sheets documents, according to Cisco Talos. Other attackers, including Russia’s state-sponsored Sandworm, are hosting their control infrastructure in blockchain-based smart contracts. Security firm Netskope recently found another campaign that used the same approach. The security company counted 5,400 sites beaconing to it, an indication of the reach and scope of that campaign. And as OS makers and defenders build new defenses, attackers keep finding documented ways to work around them. The upshot of all this is that ClickFix is a highly effective and efficient means of spreading all sorts of malware. It’s not going away, and victim-blaming or shaming only makes the problem worse. There are a fair number of plugins, standalone products, and built-in defenses that are designed to blunt the success of ClickFix attacks. For instance, BlockBlock, the software that monitors Macs for processes that seek to permanently install themselves, can block ClickFix attacks as soon as a user presses the ⌘+V keys. Ublock has been updated to do something similar. Beyond those fixes, those of us with more security training should build awareness with our less experienced neighbors, family members, and friends. The mass adoption of ClickFix demonstrates its success, and it’s not going away any time soon.

items.title: What happens when quantum mechanics and relativity meet?
items.summary: Almost a hundred years ago, physicists theorized out what free fall should do to a quantum wave. If the solution they came up with is wrong, quantum mechanics
items.text: Almost a hundred years ago, physicists theorized out what free fall should do to a quantum wave. If the solution they came up with is wrong, quantum mechanics and Einstein’s theory of gravity flatly contradict each other. But testing it has been impossible because nobody has managed to build an interferometer that could perform the necessary measurement. Now, a team led by Ron Folman, a physicist at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, with collaborators in Germany, the UK, and the US, including Nobel laureate Roger Penrose, has done it. They built a new interferometer that gives a single atom two possible paths at once: one that involves a free fall, and another where it is held perfectly still. Both paths end at the same place at the same moment, allowing the team to measure what the fall does to a wave-like property of the atom. Long time coming Ever since Galileo, physicists have known how to describe a falling object—where it is, how fast it goes, or how quickly it accelerates. Quantum mechanics, though, insists that every object is also a wave. “Every particle, doesn’t matter if it’s a car or a spaceship or an atom, is a wave,” Folman says. “Everything that is a wave, like sea waves or sound waves, goes up and down. And if you’re up or down, this is measured by something called a phase. A phase just tells you if you are at the top of the wave or at the bottom.” The wave nature of an atom shows itself only when the atom is barely moving, which only happens when it is cooled down to nearly absolute zero. For many years after theorists had first looked at this problem, this sort of temperature wasn’t an option—cooling atoms down to such temperatures only became possible in the late 1990s. “But this was just the start of the journey of this experiment,” Folman says. The second obstacle is that a phase cannot be measured on its own—it appears only when you perform a comparison. “It can only be a relative measure done by splitting a single particle into two trajectories, and then bringing the two trajectories together,” Folman says. He told Ars that this is the same logic behind the double-slit experiment, where particles fired through two narrow slits toward a background screen form an interference pattern that reveals their phase. Measuring the same thing in free fall adds another layer of complexity. “Drop a stone and after one second it is 5 meters below you,” Folman says. The question asked by the team was how to bring a wave packet that has fallen back into contact with the one that stayed behind—the same atom on the other path—so that the two can interfere. Finding the solution took his team years, even though in hindsight it sounds rather obvious. The cannon and the parachute Grabbing a falling particle and somehow bringing it back to where it started was out of the question. “Even if you could do it with some tweezer or some trap, this very violent action would create so much noise that we wouldn’t have known what is fake news and what is really the effect that we want to measure,” Folman joked. So the team figured the right way to do it would be to put an atom into a superposition of paths, where one path sees the atom thrown upward and has gravity return it to its original location. The other path isn’t really a path at all; the atom just stays where it started. “You have to shoot one with a cannon, into a ballistic motion like artillery,” Folman says. But that was just the start of the problems. The challenge, obviously, is designing a cannon that may or may not affect an atom (technically, it only affects one wave packet of the atom without affecting the other one). Then there is the issue of keeping the system in a quantum state. Interference only occurs when there is no way, even in principle, to tell which path the particle took—every measurement destroys the quantum superposition and forces the particle to behave like a localized classical object. Unfortunately, a particle returning from a ballistic flight is moving fast, while its stationary twin is not. That difference in speed is itself information about its path, so no interference pattern would appear. Atom interferometers have existed for 30 years, but none could accomplish what Folman and his colleagues wanted to do. So, they built a new one called the Quantum Galileo Interferometer (QGI). Atoms under a chip The QGI is rather tiny and relies on microwave and magnetic pulses. It uses about 20,000 rubidium atoms maintained as a Bose-Einstein condensate, held by currents in microscopic wires on a chip that hangs upside-down roughly 113 micrometers above them. A microwave pulse puts every atom into superposition of two states, where one state feels magnetic forces, and the other is blind to them. A magnetic pulse then plays the role of the cannon, kicking any magnetically sensitive atoms upward. This converts the superposition of states into a superposition of trajectories. Immediately afterward, a second microwave pulse flips the atom into the opposite state, so the superposition that’s flying upward changes into a magnetically blind one and starts falling under gravity, with no other forces influencing it. At the same time, its stationary twin becomes sensitive to magnetism, but the field is tuned so its upward force exactly cancels the atom’s weight, effectively making it hover motionless with respect to the Earth. As one of the trajectories falls back, a second magnetic pulse acts as a parachute, killing its speed just as it returns to where it started. In Folman’s experiment, at their farthest apart, the two trajectories were about 7.5 micrometers apart, and the longest flight lasted two-thousandths of a second. At the end of each run, the atoms that landed in one of the interferometer’s two exits were sorted by the phase accumulated by the falling path. As the researchers lengthened the fall, this phase increased—a behavior in line with the theory. “When somebody falls in free fall, he doesn’t feel his weight. He has no weight. Sometimes we feel [a bit of this] in an elevator that goes down very fast,” Folman says. In the quantum world, the falling path from the atom’s point of view experiences no gravity or any other force, and its wave should not pick up any extra phase. At the same time, from the laboratory’s point of view, gravity is pulling the same falling phase down, so its wave should pick up a specific amount of phase predicted by the theory. That phase difference did show up in the data. “We were able to show that the behavior of a quantum system still follows the principle of equivalence,” Folman says. “This has never been shown before—that the equivalence principle can work in a quantum system in a superposition.” In the end, the measured phase of the quantum wave sits 2.5 percent from the theoretical prediction. The result, the team argues, is a checkpoint on the border between Einstein’s relativity and quantum mechanics—two great theories in physics that stubbornly refuse to work together. “This [incompatibility] is such a problem for physicists that very smart people say that it hints that at least one of the two theories is fundamentally wrong,” Folman says. Unfortunately, the QGI did not bring us much closer to figuring out which one it might be. But Folman and his lab already have a road map they hope will get us there one day. The diamond experiment The place to look for the answers, Folman argues, is in heavier masses. Today, his lab is building a larger version of the QGI experiment that puts nanodiamonds into the same superposition—objects 10 orders of magnitude heavier than atoms, massive enough to warp spacetime around themselves. “If we put the same nanodiamond in two places, we actually have a superposition of two different curvatures of spacetime,” Folman says. And this, according to Penrose’s hypothesis, developed independently by the Hungarian physicist Lajos Diósi, is where quantum mechanics should break down. “Roger Penrose says that the Universe cannot sustain a superposition of curved spacetime. That this should collapse,” Folman says. Watching that collapse happen, or fail to, he says, would be the most direct test yet of whether gravity is quantum. The team hopes that putting nanodiamonds in superposition will become possible within the next four or five years. “It’s a very, very challenging project,” Folman says. Science Advances, 2026. DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.aec8045

items.title: LinkedIn beats "BrowserGate" lawsuits over scanning users' Chrome extensions
items.summary: LinkedIn beat two lawsuits over its practice of scanning users’ browser extensions, with a judge granting the Microsoft subsidiary’s motion to dismiss the
items.text: LinkedIn beat two lawsuits over its practice of scanning users’ browser extensions, with a judge granting the Microsoft subsidiary’s motion to dismiss the cases. The users who sued LinkedIn failed to adequately allege that they have standing to sue because neither asserted that they “had browser extensions installed that conveyed private information to LinkedIn,” ruled Judge Vince Chhabria in US District Court for the Northern District of California. In his ruling on Tuesday, Chhabria gave the plaintiffs leave to amend their complaints but said he doubts they can make a plausible case. “Given LinkedIn’s further arguments that users voluntarily download browser extensions, which by their nature intentionally expose data to websites, it seems unlikely that the plaintiffs will ever be able to allege a privacy violation, much less prevail at the end of the day,” Chhabria wrote. California residents Nicholas Farrell and Jeff Ganan separately filed class actions against LinkedIn in April, seeking to represent themselves and other LinkedIn users. Ganan’s attorney, J.R. Howell, said he is evaluating whether to bring the claims in a California state court, which has different requirements on standing, or to appeal the US district court ruling in the US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. “The federal court determined that it lacked jurisdiction to hear the LinkedIn users’ claims,” Howell told Ars today. “The court did not adjudicate whether LinkedIn’s surveillance practices were lawful. The ruling is not a vindication of the mass surveillance program alleged in our complaint.” “BrowserGate” stems from dispute over scraping As we wrote in April , the plaintiffs filed their lawsuits after a report alleged that “LinkedIn Is illegally searching your computer.” LinkedIn did not deny that it scans browsers to identify extensions and already disclosed in its privacy policy that it uses cookies and similar technologies to collect information about each user’s “web browser and add-ons.” The so-called “BrowserGate” report was issued by a German entity called Fairlinked , which describes itself as a trade association and advocacy group for commercial LinkedIn users. It appeared to be run by the same people behind Teamfluence, an Estonian software company that sued LinkedIn in Munich after its CEO was banned by LinkedIn. Howell, Ganan’s lawyer, also serves as counsel for Fairlinked in the US. In a June court filing , Howell wrote that “my investigative work with Fairlinked e.V. and Browsergate occurred before my office filed the Ganan complaint.” LinkedIn said in a motion to dismiss that it uses detection systems to identify the type of automated scraping and bot activity that Teamfluence was deploying. LinkedIn told the court: Teamfluence, an Estonian platform, is one of those groups that traffics in scraping. It markets a Google Chrome browser plug-in designed to “[i]dentify 100% of your LinkedIn traffic.” LinkedIn caught it and banned its CEO from the platform, leading to a legal dispute in Germany. A German tribunal recently determined that “[t]he ‘Teamfluence’ software violates [LinkedIn’s User Agreement],” and that LinkedIn’s “suspending the Claimants’ user accounts is objectively justified overall and not arbitrary.” Judge: Plaintiffs did not allege concrete harm After the German court order, the Teamfluence-linked group called Fairlinked emerged with the BrowserGate report, which attracted coverage on a number of tech news sites. “No surprise: the founder of Teamfluence sits on Fairlinked’s board,” LinkedIn’s motion said. “Having been caught for scraping, and held to have violated LinkedIn’s terms, he has now embarked on an international retaliation campaign by manufacturing a fake privacy controversy. But it is Teamfluence that is scraping data without consent.” Teamfluence’s CEO and founder is named Steven Morell. Chhabria’s ruling said that neither Farrell nor Ganan “alleges that they, specifically, had browser extensions installed that conveyed private information to LinkedIn. Ganan never alleges that he had any extensions installed at all. Farrell alleges that he ‘has long had several browser extensions installed,’ and that, in general, browser extensions ‘often reveal sensitive private information about its users,’ but he never alleges that one of his own browser extensions revealed such information.” The judge said the “allegations are insufficient to confer standing because only ‘those plaintiffs who have been concretely harmed by a defendant’s statutory violation may sue that private defendant over that violation in federal court.’ Identifying categories of private information that hypothetically could be revealed by surveillance of browser extensions is not enough to allege standing ‘particularized to a plaintiff’s circumstances,’” as precedent requires. Ganan argued in a filing that the harm is “the unpermitted probe, not its yield,” but Chhabria wrote that “a plaintiff must identify ’embarrassing, invasive, or otherwise private information collected by’ the defendant.” Lawyer vows to continue case LinkedIn’s motion to dismiss said it uses detection tools “to identify whether a visitor to the platform is operating a browser extension that could threaten the security and integrity of the platform,” and that “LinkedIn detects information that browser extensions openly provide to all websites in order to interact with them. The information is publicly available and in no way private. And LinkedIn’s right to detect this information is disclosed and agreed to by all its members. So is LinkedIn’s right to use security-focused vendors to detect and prevent potential abuse.” LinkedIn said that some Chrome browser extensions extract job listings and related data from the company’s website, and that LinkedIn’s terms prohibit extensions that scrape or copy data from the site. LinkedIn’s “rich platform and robust community make LinkedIn a target for opportunistic software developers who seek to scrape its data for their own purposes,” the company said. Howell told Ars today that the Ganan lawsuit “alleges that LinkedIn deployed code without users’ consent to surveil their internal computing environments, collect information, and route data to third parties.” “The companies developing and deploying these technologies should not get to decide, on their own, the boundaries of our privacy,” Howell said. “As their ability to observe and profile people expands, meaningful consent and judicial scrutiny become more important. … We intend to pursue these claims in a forum that can adjudicate them on their merits.” We also contacted Farrell’s lawyers about the judge’s ruling and will update this article if we get a response. Although Farrell’s lawyers don’t appear to have coordinated directly with Fairlinked, the claims in their lawsuit were based largely on the group’s BrowserGate report.

items.title: Europe will go it alone on Venus mission after NASA yanks radar instrument
items.summary: The European Space Agency is moving “full steam ahead” with development of a robotic mission to Venus after NASA officials determined they were unlikely to
items.text: The European Space Agency is moving “full steam ahead” with development of a robotic mission to Venus after NASA officials determined they were unlikely to fulfill a commitment to provide a US-built radar instrument for the spacecraft, the mission’s project scientist said. The European orbiter, named Envision, will map the Venusian surface at 10 times higher resolution than the last radar mission sent to Venus by NASA in the 1990s. The planet is enshrouded in a blanket of thick clouds of sulfuric acid, rendering its mysterious surface unseen by optical cameras in orbit. Radar is the most effective way to penetrate the clouds of Venus to reveal the terrain below, and scientists will use Envision to look for signs of active volcanism. NASA and ESA signed a memorandum of understanding in 2024 outlining their partnership on Envision. NASA agreed to supply a US-made synthetic aperture radar instrument, Envision’s primary means of mapping the surface of Venus, along with providing tracking and communications support through NASA’s Deep Space Network. In exchange, ESA would include US researchers on Envision’s science team. Europe would build the Envision spacecraft and the rest of its science instruments and provide the launch on an Ariane 6 rocket. But NASA’s budget for science missions is under the gun from the Trump administration, which proposed slashing the agency’s science funding nearly in half in fiscal years 2026 and 2027. Congress rejected most of the cuts in 2026, when lawmakers passed a budget with $2.54 billion for NASA’s planetary science division, far above the White House’s request, but about $220 million shy of last year’s funding. That saved several key science missions from the chopping block, including one of NASA’s own Venus missions, called DAVINCI, designed to send an entry probe into the planet’s crushing atmosphere. But the shortfall is forcing NASA managers to make tough decisions . The primary targets for cuts in science are NASA’s funding for operating missions, especially those well beyond their original design lives, and support for partnerships on international missions. Reneging on a pledge Most prominent among the cuts in the latter category are NASA’s contributions to three European-led science missions. Two of the missions are big, new space-based observatories, LISA and New Athena. LISA will be the first space mission to measure gravitational waves, ripples in the fabric of spacetime emanating from cataclysmic cosmic events like mergers of black holes. New Athena will be the largest X-ray telescope ever built, a successor to NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, still operational after launching in 1999. Before NASA’s contributions were in doubt, LISA and New Athena were on track for launches in the late 2030s. But the most pressing impact for ESA is how to fill the void left by NASA in the Envision mission, which was supposed to launch in 2031. NASA and ESA signed an agreement in early 2024 detailing each partner’s role on Envision, and contracts were awarded for construction of the Envision spacecraft and its instruments. NASA had spent more than $50 million on its contributions to the mission as of 2025, when the Trump administration first proposed canceling it. With NASA’s fulfillment of its part of the agreement in doubt, ESA officials issued contracts to begin technology development on a European radar payload for Envision. Industrial teams in the United Kingdom and Italy are now studying radar designs under contract with ESA, with the goal of delivering a radar for Envision with similar capabilities as the NASA-funded radar, which was to be built at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California. “We don’t know what the final design will be, b ut we have the same requirements, so we’re expecting that we can do exactly the same science,” said Anne Grete Straume-Lindner, ESA’s project scientist for Envision, in a presentation at the Europlanet Science Congress. “ We’ll have the same modes, but in detail, of course, there can be differences.” Carole Mundell, ESA’s director of science, told Ars earlier this year that the agency’s 23 member states committed “unprecedented” funding for ESA science at a meeting of government ministers last year. The member states agreed to increase ESA’s science budget by 3.5 percent per year through 2028, plus inflation. Still, ESA’s science budget is a fraction of that of NASA, averaging out to about 750 million euros (less than $900 million) each year. That’s enough to start work on a European radar for Envision, even as ESA still awaits a formal notification from NASA on the status of its contribution to the mission. “NASA conversations with ESA regarding Envision are ongoing,” a NASA spokesperson said. But time is of the essence if Envision is to launch in the early 2030s. ESA officials have already delayed Envision’s launch by one year to 2032 to give teams in Europe more time to deliver the radar. “ At the moment, we are finalizing our agreement with NASA, but it is looking like they are not able to provide the radar,” Straume-Lindner said in response to a question from Ars. “So that is why we are going full steam ahead with the European solution.” Cancellations and delays A complementary mission to Envision, NASA’s VERITAS radar orbiter, was supposed to launch in the late 2020s, but funding woes at NASA and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory forced a delay until no earlier than 2031. Its development remains in limbo. The DAVINCI mission, led by NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center, continues working toward a launch in the early 2030s . The work of the Venus Science Coordination group, established jointly by NASA and ESA, has also been suspended due to “changes to the budgetary situation in the US,” Straume-Lindner said. Meanwhile, ESA is also assessing how it can fill the roles of NASA on LISA and New Athena. On LISA, NASA was to provide lasers and ultra-stable telescopes for the mission’s three formation-flying spacecraft. The US space agency was on the hook for X-ray sensor hardware, a cryocooler, and a vibration isolation system for New Athena. The Trump administration also sought to cancel NASA’s role in ESA’s Rosalind Franklin rover mission to Mars, set for launch in 2028. NASA has a long-standing agreement with ESA to pay for the launch of the European-built rover, and funding restored by Congress last year allowed the space agency to sign a contract with SpaceX to launch Rosalind Franklin in 2028. “ESA is a very reliable partner, and we always deliver on our commitments and our promises, and we appreciate the difficulty that they’re in right now,” Mundell said, referring to NASA. Europe has other places to look for cooperation in space, but NASA is the agency’s most enduring partner. In human spaceflight, ESA and NASA cooperate closely on the International Space Station and the Orion spacecraft used for Artemis missions to the Moon. ESA launched its first 50-50 joint science mission with China earlier this year. The SMILE spacecraft, built in China and launched by Europe’s Vega rocket, is studying the connection between the solar wind and Earth. The first ESA instrument to land on the Moon arrived on the lunar surface in 2024 aboard China’s Chang’e 6 mission. Mundell said China has invited ESA to join more Chinese-led science missions. “That is something that we’re exploring,” she said.

items.title: Panic builds over bankrupt Spirit’s looming data sale to Google
items.summary: Doug Kreuzkamp was shocked when news outlets reported that Google won an auction to buy a huge amount of operational data as part of Spirit Airlines’
items.text: Doug Kreuzkamp was shocked when news outlets reported that Google won an auction to buy a huge amount of operational data as part of Spirit Airlines’ bankruptcy proceedings. Kreuzkamp founded a startup called Springshot in 2011, which created a widely used proprietary platform that helps humans and AI systems improve airline efficiency and quickly solve logistics problems so flights can stay on time and airlines can operate as smoothly as possible. Hundreds of airports use it globally. Springshot powered Spirit’s technology stack for the last three years, right up to the “very last flight,” Kreuzkamp told Ars. Yet his company got no notice when Spirit prepared to auction off a massive dataset that he thinks likely improperly includes a substantial amount of data and intellectual property (IP) that Springshot owns—not Spirit. In a limited objection filed last month, Springshot argued that Spirit’s sale agreement does not make it clear what data is being sold. It only vaguely references categories of data that would possibly rope in Springshot data, including “productivity and collaboration data,” “core business systems and business application data,” and “workflow and process data.” “This expansive definition does nothing to differentiate between Springshot’s intellectual property that exists within Spirit’s data repositories and systems, but Spirit does not own, and Spirit data that it actually owns and has the capacity to sell,” Springshot argued. Springshot urged the court to pause Spirit’s data sale until a transparent forensic process establishes that none of the data Google is grabbing is actually owned by third parties. If the bankruptcy court does not “pump the brakes,” it risks sanctioning an “unauthorized acquisition and use of trade secrets” that could doom startups, Springshot alleged. In an email to Ars, Springshot summarized its fears as the court possibly creating “a precedent where startups see massive amounts of IP transferred to the world’s richest and most monopolistic companies via bankruptcy courts.” “Bankruptcy cannot become the new land grab for AI,” Kreuzkamp told Ars. “The possession of IP is not ownership.” Asked for comment, Google’s spokesperson declined to discuss mounting objections and repeated a prior statement provided to Ars that did not address any of the concerns raised. “We acquired part of an enterprise dataset from Spirit Airlines, which can be helpful in improving our products and AI models,” Google’s spokesperson said. “We will not receive any personal information from this dataset.” Google may use Springshot data to make AI rival It seems likely that a wide range of Spirit vendors could be in the same spot as Springshot, Kreuzkamp suspects, and his firm is not the only one complaining. Citing Springshot’s concerns in a separate objection , the International Aero Engines LLC and the IAE International Aero Engines AG alleged that the dataset might also include its proprietary commercial information, technical data, and financial data. Both vendors cited confidentiality provisions in Spirit agreements that appear to have been completely ignored in the push to get the data sale approved. Top concerns are that proprietary data could be transferred to Google without consent, giving firms no chance to guard against Google—or a third party later gaining access to the data—infringing ownership rights and exposing trade secrets. Both vendors said they risked irreparable harm through the sale to Google and then again through possible resales to future third parties. For Springshot, it also seems possible that Google could use its valuable IP to create a rival product. In August, just a week before the controversial Spirit auction, Europe’s largest airline, Ryanair, announced a five-year partnership with Google. Under the deal, Ryanair will share operational data to improve Gemini Enterprise tools. That “is precisely the function Springshot served for Spirit,” the startup said in a footnote in its objection, while alleging that “Springshot’s data may be among the most AI-relevant assets to be purchased.” As Springshot argued: “Should the sale proceed without such safeguards, and should Google obtain Springshot’s intellectual property and ingest that data, Springshot would forfeit the value of its technology it has spent 15 years developing. That existential threat is only amplified by the fact that Google has recently announced its desire to operationalize its own AI platform for airline operations, placing it in direct competition with Springshot.” Adam Schwartz, a privacy litigation director for a digital rights nonprofit called the Electronic Frontier Foundation, told Ars that allowing Google to buy this dataset via bankruptcy proceedings is unusual. “This is the first time I am aware of so public a bankruptcy proceeding regarding whether a bankrupt company may sell off the personal data it has amassed as an asset in bankruptcy,” Schwartz said. “It is also the first time I am aware of a company seeking to sell its employees’ data (as opposed to its customers’ data) as an asset in bankruptcy.” Kreuzkamp is worried that because bankruptcy courts have not deeply considered this issue before, the system is just not set up to protect vendors like his company. In the past, it was straightforward to determine who owned an asset. Consider how Spirit is selling airplanes, which bills of sale clearly demonstrate that it owns, he said. His experience suggests that when it comes to digital assets, courts don’t have the proper notice provisions that are necessary to ensure vendors can advocate for IP to be segregated from sales, should purchases like Google’s become the norm. “Our main concern with everything is if you want startups to continue building, you need to protect what they built,” Kreuzkamp told Ars. “If they spent 15 years building IP, that IP should not be misappropriated because their customer went bankrupt.” Springshot and the IAE objectors both want the court to require Spirit to segregate any proprietary vendor data before approving the sale to Google. Springshot argued that it should include any data or information generated by its service or software, including data “likely commingled with much of Spirit’s own operational data (like its employees’ emails, chat histories, etc.).” “To ensure Springshot’s intellectual property is not among the data acquired by Google (or any other potential buyer) a forensic process is necessary to first identify, and then segregate, Springshot’s intellectual property from that actually owned by Spirit,” Springshot argued. Kreuzkamp told Ars that Springshot engaged with Spirit every day before it shut down. “We were very tightly coupled with them, did a lot of great work helping that airline,” he said. “And so, I know there are tens of thousands of emails and documents that I’m sure are in their servers.” Pilots warn of public harms from sale If Spirit is forced to segregate a large chunk of data, the value of the dataset may substantially depreciate for Google. In its sale agreement, Google stipulated that Spirit ensure that “no portion of the Assets has been deleted, modified, or removed,” other than through planned processes like the deidentification of customers’ personal data and “de minimis” removals preserving privileged materials. Kreuzkamp told Ars that prior to reading the Spirit-Google sale agreement, he assumed that if one of the companies he partnered with became insolvent, that either vendor data would be destroyed or that agreements would be honored to prevent transfers to third parties. On September 16, there will be a hearing where the court will mull objections to the sale. Along with vendors, unions and groups representing many former Spirit employees have joined flight attendants who quickly opposed the sale out of fears that Google or a third party could possibly link them to scrubbed data. Troublingly, the sale agreement only required de-identification of customer personal data, and former Spirit workers worried that Google’s AI system may combine confidential worker data in ways that may expose information that they might not want public. As groups representing machinists, aerospace workers, and transport workers noted , workers aren’t even aware of all the risks, since “the proposed sale raises novel technological and legal concerns on very short notice.” Seemingly, not even Spirit knows the “ultimate uses” to which the data “may be put after it is sold and processed through artificial intelligence,” they warned. Schwartz told Ars that Spirit should have gotten consent from workers before selling 80,000 email accounts, 100 million emails, 20 million SharePoint documents, and 500 million Teams messages. “My top concern is that data privacy is a fundamental human right, enjoyed for example by employees in relation to their employers,” Schwartz said. “This includes the norm that data collected from a person for one reason should not be used or disclosed for another reason without first getting their opt-in consent. Therefore, it is the Spirit Airline employees themselves who should be making the decision whether they want to bear the risk to their privacy of their emails being turned into AI training data.” Some former workers are alarmed that the data sale could possibly harm the public. Most ominously, the Air Line Pilots Association, International warned that if Google’s AI system re-identifies pilots in the data set, airways could become more dangerous. Flight safety programs depend on pilots feeling comfortable sharing in-depth incident reports without fear that confidential information may become public, the Federal Aviation Administration has found. Therefore, any “disclosure of confidential flight operations data through the Sale Agreement can be expected to chill voluntary compliance by pilots across the industry as it becomes known that such data can be sold to third parties with no expertise or interest in aviation safety and presumably included in databases accessible by the public using artificial intelligence software,” the association warned. Late Google rival vows to resolve objections Last week, an AI training data lab, Micro1, put in a last-minute competing bid that it claims resolves all objections to the data sale. Outbidding Google by 25 percent, Micro1 offered $12.5 million in cash, while promising that if debtors pick Micro1 over Google, the bankruptcy proceedings can avoid any further delays. However, Micro1’s plan notably includes de-identifying the data in-house, which Spirit debtors were opposed to in the auction process. Spirit even chose a lower second bid should the Google sale fall through because the de-identification was completed by independent third parties. It seems, then, that even if the late bid is considered, it’s less likely to tempt debtors. Additionally, Micro1’s claims to resolve all objections may be somewhat exaggerated. In Springshot’s case, Micro1 does not promise to segregate IP, trade secrets, or proprietary data. Instead, Micro1 only says that it will not use Springshot data to create a rival product or ever sell the data to a would-be rival. Ars could not reach Micro1’s lawyers for comment, but the data lab said it plans to attend the upcoming hearing to entice debtors to take their offer. Kreuzkamp told Ars that he appreciates that Micro1 acknowledges Springshot’s concerns, but his objective remains scrubbing Spirit’s dataset of any data that Springshot owns. His company’s lawyers have been in contact with Spirit debtors’ legal team and plan to defend Springshot’s proprietary data at the upcoming hearing. They feel confident the court will take their concerns seriously. But there are no guarantees, as the bankruptcy court prepares to approve this unusual sale. Kreuzkamp said it remains unclear what process a bankrupt company like Spirit should be taking to “ensure that it extricates everything that is proprietary from a dataset.” “I just think it’s a very complex issue when it comes to extricating the data that’s owned by somebody else,” Kreuzkamp said. However, now’s the time to do it, he suggested, since “once you throw data into an AI model, it’s impossible to trace what the model did with that.”

items.title: 首个走进联合国的中国教育 Agent，正在打开下一个 Token 入口
items.summary: 过去两年，AI 行业一直在寻找 Coding 之后的下一个高价值入口。办公软件，争夺文档、表格和日程；智能硬件争夺真实世界的数据。 教育可能是一个长期被低估的答案。 教育 AI 已经开始进入规模化应用阶段。OECD TALIS 2024 显示，约三分之一的初中教师已经在工作中使用 AI；在使用者中，64%
items.text: 过去两年，AI 行业一直在寻找 Coding 之后的下一个高价值入口。办公软件，争夺文档、表格和日程；智能硬件争夺真实世界的数据。 教育可能是一个长期被低估的答案。 教育 AI 已经开始进入规模化应用阶段。OECD TALIS 2024 显示，约三分之一的初中教师已经在工作中使用 AI；在使用者中，64% 会用它生成教案或课堂活动。 设计一门课程，需要理解学习目标、检索和核验材料、组织知识顺序，再生成讲解、幻灯片、互动与反馈， 它与软件工程一样，拥有漫长的任务链条，也需要在多轮修改中不断调用模型。 在教育场景里，AI 需要走出之前的一问一答的简单模式，转而去实现一整套知识生产工作。 9 月 8 日，巴黎，联合国教科文组织总部，在 Digital Learning Week 2026 的一场官方活动中，清华大学教育学院张羽教授和于济凡助理教授，用 90 分钟向来自不同国家和地区的教师、校长、教育管理者和政策制定者介绍 OpenMAIC。 现场参与者还将自己的教学主题交给 Agent，亲手生成课程。 这是首个登上联合国舞台的中国教育 Agent 团队，为全球 AI 竞争提供了一个新坐标： 当大模型竞争走出参数榜单，中国团队开始向外输出一套组织知识、设计课程的方法。 OpenMAIC 源自清华大学教育学院与计算机系联合团队于 2024 年启动的 MAIC 项目，并于 2026 年 3 月开源。截至 8 月 20 日，平台已有超过 55 万名创作者，累计交互超过 3400 万次，覆盖 154 个国家和地区。 8 月 28 日，OpenMAIC 升级为v1.0 正式版——Agent驱动的专业工作台，其最新数据显示平台累计消耗 883B Token；近 30 天消耗 68B Token，环比增长 203%。 更关键是升级前后的用量对比，旧版 OpenMAIC 生成一个互动课堂平均消耗约 35.8 万 Token；Agent 专业工作台的一个完整创作任务平均消耗约 362.5 万 Token，约为此前的 10.1 倍，背后平均调用模型 74.3 次。反映了产品从课堂生成器向完整课程工作台演进后，单次任务链路和模型调用深度的变化。 需求侧的普及，与产品侧从单次内容生成向完整课程生产的深化，正在同时发生。OpenMAIC v1.0 单次任务 Token 用量的增长，呈现的正是后一种变化： 当 AI 开始承担规划、检索、生成、互动与修改，教育也正在成为承接长链条 Agent 任务的重要入口，显露出成为 Token 经济时代又一重要应用入口的潜力。 Coding 之后，为什么是教育 Token 曾经只是大模型账单上的计量单位。Agent 出现以后，它也开始衡量 AI 究竟有多深入真实任务。 Coding 最先验证了这条路径。软件工程要求模型理解需求、拆解任务、调用工具并反复调试； 当 AI 从聊天框进入长链条工作流，Token 才真正成为生产资料 。 办公 Agent 正在争夺文档、表格和日程入口，但教学工作中的办公，只能称得上是教育 Token 的外围，要真正进入教学，需要为不同的人构建完整的学习体验。 这也意味着，教育场景有着相似的结构，同样是一项长链条、多轮次任务： 确定目标，检索材料，设计知识顺序，再生成幻灯片、声音、互动与反馈；课程还要随教师判断和学习者反应持续修改。 显然，教育场景还有更多可以探索的空间。 从旧版到 v1.0，单个任务 Token 用量的变化，对应的是模型接手了更长的任务链：课程规划、素材处理、生成、修改和复用都被纳入同一工作流。教育 Agent 由此具备了与 Coding Agent 相似的产业条件： 需求足够刚性，链路足够长，也能持续调用模型与工具。 教育 Agent 的战场，不在课件，而在工作流 过去的教育数字化首先解决了存储和分发，课程生产仍高度依赖教师个人：怎样选材料、排难度、提问题，再根据反馈修改，这些经验很难装进模板。 生成式 AI 降低了制作课件的门槛，也暴露出新的问题：让 AI 理解材料、遵循教学方法、完成多轮修改，并把有效做法带到下一门课， 教育 Agent 的竞争因此从「生成了什么」，转向「如何稳定生产」。 OpenMAIC v1.0 选择切入这条生产链，专业工作台用持续对话承接课程目标、受众、时长和素材；Agent 可以调用搜索、幻灯片、Quiz、互动页面、声音与项目式学习等工具，并在同一个任务里继续修改。 这条生产链有着巨大的应用空间，打开了存量知识的第二条生命线 。对教育行业来说，可以对旧教案焕新；对内容行业来说，过往报道和文章不再止于一次阅读，而可以继续生长为可操作、可反馈、可迭代的学习产品。 我们把一篇关于电影制式与影厅选择的旧报道交给它，原有文字和图表被重新组织为讲解、互动与小测，课程还生成了一个购票决策模型，让学习者按预算、视觉、听觉和舒适度比较影厅。 旧内容由此获得了新的使用方式，也说明 专业工作台处理的对象已经从单次生成，转向一项可以反复编辑的内容工程 。 工作流解决了课程如何完成，Skill 决定了复用的效率。OpenMAIC 把费曼学习法、螺旋式课程等方法封装为 Skill，也允许用户制作自己的 Skill。原本隐性的设计经验由此可以被描述、调用和迁移，逐步沉淀为可复用的生产资产。 在「普通人如何看懂一座建筑」这一主题里，Agent 自动检索建筑图片，从斗拱、穹顶等具体对象切入，组织出「观察—提问—验证」的学习路径。 更进一步，OpenMAIC 通过标准化的 Skill 与 SDK 接入 DeepSeek Harness、Codex、WorkBuddy 等 Agent 工作台，课程生成因此可以成为通用 Agent 的一项能力。模型负责理解和推理，Harness 提供调用工具、保存进度与连续执行任务的环境，OpenMAIC 则提供课程生产能力。 ▲ 通过 Claude Code 调用 OpenMAIC 对于学习者，复杂知识获得了可交互的解释；对于开发者，教育能力也开始像搜索、写作和编程工具一样被嵌入不同场景。 从专业工作台到 Skill，再到 Harness 与 SDK，OpenMAIC v1.0 增加的不只是三组功能，整体看来，它重新划定了产品边界：从一个课程生成工具，走向课程生产系统，并进一步成为 Agent 生态中的教育能力层。 走进联合国，中国开源的是一种教育能力 随着基础模型逐渐趋同，教育 Agent 的竞争也会从单点功能转向工作流与生态。谁能让更多教学法被复用、让更多开发者接入、让课程能力在不同 Harness 之间流动，谁就更有机会定义教育内容的新生产标准，并承接由此产生的 Token 消耗，开源由此也成为一种产业策略。 OpenMAIC 选择开源并保持模型与 Harness ，让学校、教师和开发者可以替换模型与材料，进行本地部署和二次开发，让同一套工具适配不同语言、文化与教学目标。   如果拆开教育 Agent 的价值链，上游是提供推理与多模态能力的基础模型，中游负责组织任务、调用工具和沉淀教学方法，下游则连接学校、教师与具体课程。模型并不稀缺，能够把模型能力稳定转化为课程的生产系统，才是现阶段的关键中间层，OpenMAIC 正在争取的正是这个位置。   这也是 OpenMAIC 走进 UNESCO 更大的意义，对资源有限的学校和教师，开放的课程生产能力有机会继续降低优质内容的门槛；对 AI 教育行业，开放让技术路径和教学假设可以被检验、比较与修正。 它同时呈现了中国 AI 竞争力的另一种形态：模型参数和榜单展示技术能力，开源应用则把能力变成全球教育工作者可以使用、修改和再创造的工具。中国团队输出的不仅是一款产品，也是一套建设 AI 原生学习环境的方法。 Coding 已经让人们看到，Agent 可以成为专业工作的新入口。接下来，当 AI 开始持续组织知识、调用教学方法并适应不同学习者，教育 Token 的市场才刚刚打开。 #欢迎关注爱范儿官方微信公众号：爱范儿（微信号：ifanr），更多精彩内容第一时间为您奉上。

items.title: 硬氪专访丨对话iRobot：扫地机行业到了纠偏时刻
items.summary: 时隔多年，iRobot再次站上了国际消费电子展的舞台。 9月初，柏林IFA展会上，iRobot发布了新旗舰Roomba875，并把大量展区留给了一台尚未命名的子母双机概念机。这次重返国际顶级展会。官方将其定义为“把品牌重新带回世界舞台”的信号：“这个品牌带着更好的产品、更好的姿态回来了。”
items.text: 时隔多年，iRobot再次站上了国际消费电子展的舞台。 9月初，柏林IFA展会上，iRobot发布了新旗舰Roomba875，并把大量展区留给了一台尚未命名的子母双机概念机。这次重返国际顶级展会。官方将其定义为“把品牌重新带回世界舞台”的信号：“这个品牌带着更好的产品、更好的姿态回来了。” 这轮回归带着明确的自我修正意味。过去几年，iRobot留给外界的印象并不算好：手握3000多项专利却长期不落地，一个平台沿用多年不迭代，被贴上“保守”的标签。而在受访负责人看来，行业同样到了一个需要纠偏的节点——扫地机器人全球平均渗透率只有10%出头，行业却在不断卷单一参数，把消费者越带越远。 一些数据已经在验证纠偏的价值。iRobot日本市场市占率从年初的约40%，到上个月已经回到72%。本次IFA展会上，单一欧洲国家的经销商已经为iRobot产品准备了5000万欧元的投入预算。 硬氪在IFA现场与iRobot联席CEO李昊聊了近一个小时，从发展战略、产品理念、业务策略，到中国消费者变化、渠道竞争与团队配合，聊聊一个老品牌在新时代的新思考。以下是经过编辑整理的对话实录。 回归国际展会 硬氪：这次参加IFA，对iRobot来说有什么战略意义？想通过这场展会传递什么信号？ 李昊： 这个展会对我们来说有两个主要意义。一个是发布产品本身，昨天刚上市的新旗舰875，以及首次亮相的概念机；另一个是，这个品牌蛮久没有出现在各类国际展会上了，所以参展本身也是一个把品牌重新带回世界舞台的信号——告诉大家，我们回来了，这个品牌现在带着更好的产品、更好的姿态回来了。 产品理念上，无论是旗舰875还是概念产品，核心想讲的就一句话：不要去卷参数，回到产品本身。对消费者来说，无论功能说得多么花哨，到最后其实就是两个点：清洁力怎么样？在好的清洁力之下，覆盖率够不够？我们想把清洁能力和覆盖能力真正提升上去，给消费者一个回归产品本身的体验。 硬氪：以全新的姿态回来面对消费者，想给他们讲一个什么样的故事？ 李昊： 我想讲的不一样，是建立在一个不变的愿景之上的。iRobot的愿景我一开始就非常认同：让机器人去做人类不该做、不想做的事，把人解放出来，把时间真正还给消费者，让他们去做自己认为真正重要的事情。 要变的是什么呢？十几年前，iRobot完成了这个行业第一次大变革——从“没有家庭机器人”到让大众认知家庭机器人。现在我想做的是第二个变革：现在有家庭机器人了，但消费者对它们并不完全满意，渗透率也没上去。我要做的是让家庭机器人变成像大家电一样、真正根植到用户心中的产品。 这就是为什么我反复强调要抛去噱头、回到体验。你看洗衣机、电视，消费者买的时候已经很清楚自己要什么了，扫地机还没有——行业去卷吸力，标30KPa、40KPa、50KPa，会误导消费者以为那就是清洁力。其实行业内的人都知道不是。消费者现在缺的，就是一个“什么代表清洁力”的认知，我们希望把这个认知带回来。 不靠单一参数，靠系统式的组合 硬氪：以新的品牌形象登陆欧洲市场，我们跟别家真正的差异化在哪？核心竞争力体现在什么方面？ 李昊： 回到消费者能理解的两个点：一是更强的清洁力，这是产品存在的核心价值；二是覆盖率——清洁力再强，到不了某些地方，就等于没清洁。 尤其对中国的消费者，他们买扫地机的客单价是偏高的，说明大家愿意为这件事买单，那我们更不能让消费者失望。如果消费者买回去发现扫地机是一个并不值得买的东西，他们就不再愿意买，渗透率就永远上不去。 硬氪：聊聊875吧，作为这次带来的旗舰产品，它想传递什么？ 李昊： 875就是基于我刚才说的那套理念开发的。旗舰该有的智能性能、运动性能都有，我不赘述，核心讲对消费者最有价值的点。 第一，干清洁。大吸力不是完全没用，但它是流量和吸力之间的一个平衡。我们不去管参数标多少，而是找最好的流量和吸力平衡点，让扫地机在地毯上有最好的清洁能力。找到平衡之后还有个问题——流量会散失，因为扫地机不会完全贴死在地面。怎么减少流量损失？靠整个主动密封装置的设计。875的密封系统能大幅减少流量损失，地毯除尘率基本对标头部吸尘器品牌，而不是跟扫地机比。 这个点以前大家觉得只对欧美重要，现在要加上中国了——中国现在的装修趋势是意式，而意式装修里很重要的一个元素就是客厅的大地毯。中国消费者对地毯本来就认知偏弱，很多人纠结“要不要买地毯”卡在“怎么清洁”，我们希望把这个问题交给875去处理。 第二，湿清洁。这是中国和欧洲消费者最关心的，尤其是中国家庭油污很常见。油污最好的清洁方式就是常识：清洁剂加高温。我们做的就是用热雾加清洁液去融化油污，再靠一个很强的滚筒完成“洗涤机一样的清洁能力”。我不会刻意强调“我给了300RPM”，但转速确实关键——扫地机经过地面的时间就那么多，转速高意味着多擦几遍；再加上行业内最大的滚筒接触面积，单位时间内摩擦走过的长度最长，重污才能在融化的基础上被真正擦干净。 你会发现很多时候它都是一个组合。像iRobot最早开创、到现在所有竞争对手都在用的三段式清洁——边刷先聚拢、中扫往上赶、风机再吸进去——干扫是这样，湿清洁我们也做成多段式的组合。我们不靠单一参数，靠系统式的组合把清洁力拉到最高。 硬氪：以您的产品技术背景看，一个好的扫地机应该是什么样？ 李昊： 四个点，清洁力+覆盖率+智能性+免维护。清洁力和覆盖率，解决的是“你要把活干了”的问题；智能性解决的是未来方向，一方面辅助前两点，比如用AI做多次复拖识别，另一方面往服务机器人、家庭管家的方向演进，这是智能性的战略价值；最后是免维护——消费者除了要尝鲜，他要的是省心，要的是一个成熟稳定的大家电。 你看洗衣机、电视、冰箱，需要维护的都很少。扫地机什么时候能到这个程度？我在看任何一个产品规划、技术规划的时候都会问：这个规划是否落在四个点里、是否解决里面的核心问题？如果不解决，那可能你做的就是一个伪命题。 扫地机替代洗地机的可能性出现了 硬氪：这次展会上很大的面积给了概念型产品，它在你们的产品序列里意味着什么？ 李昊：还是从清洁力和覆盖率讲。875在湿清洁上已经有很多突破，但清洁力还有继续向上的空间，而这个空间需要的是体积。为什么手持洗地机吸面条很轻松？因为它长，可以装一个非常强的风机，这是扫地机以前很难做到的。那把扫地机做高一点，是不是就具备了这样的能力？这台概念机的母机主机，就预留了进一步大幅提升清洁力的空间——我会把机身做高，去容纳更强劲的风机。  iRobot概念机 这里有个很关键的巧思：母机的占地面积跟现在的扫地机基站没什么区别。我们调研过，对大部分空间敏感的家庭来说，大家缺的不是垂直空间，缺的是投影面积。所以它不额外占你的地，却开拓了大幅提升清洁力的可能性——相当于一个会移动的基站，加上更强的清洁能力。 第二个是子机，核心解决覆盖率。两个场景：一个是错层，这对所有扫地机器人来说目前都是无解的，我们的方案把子机带到不同层去；另一个就是你提过的“桌子腿问题”——大家做测试的时候把餐桌摆得规规整整，看着空间挺大，但真实生活里吃完饭凳子是要推回桌底的，凳腿和桌腿交叉在一起，没有任何算法能穷举这种可能性，这时候就看两件事：算法对不同场景的适应能力，以及物理层面有没有最好的空间适应性。子机要提供的，就是比任何单一机器人更好的通过性，把覆盖率的“最后一公里”补齐。 比如一个家庭，全球平均覆盖率如果假设在80%，我们能不能通过更小更薄、子母机、更高阶的越障，做到90%、95%？在这个基础上再做更深度清洁，这就是母机存在的价值。所以Roomba Duo不是一个边缘场景的产品，它是把“清洁力+覆盖率”这套系统能力再往上推一层的产品。 硬氪：展厅里那个吸面条的演示还挺让人新奇的。 李昊： 吸面条本身确实是个吸眼球的展示，日常很少有人会吸到面条，但它核心要突出的是重污清洁能力。吸面条是洗地机常用的性能展示，扫地机行业以前没有，因为扫地机的重污能力还没到这个地步。现在我们把扫地机做到跟洗地机一样的清洁力，再把覆盖率覆盖到原来需要手动清洁的边角——扫地机真正替代洗地机的可能性就出现了，消费者不用再买那么多产品，一个省心的机器就能把活干完。 核心是做每个地区的本地化 硬氪：站在海外市场的角度，iRobot这种成熟国际品牌，你们在品牌打法上有什么心得？ 李昊： 最关键的一点，是你得理解海外每个地区的消费者——这跟我做产品的思路一致，回到消费者视角。你刚才用了“出海”这个词，其实比较笼统，这个世界上不是只有中国和外国，而是有很多国家，核心是要做每个地区的本地化。 拿日本举例，日本年初市占率大概40%，上个月已经回到72%。怎么做到的？从产品到营销，都要理解日本消费者到底要什么。日本家庭空间偏小，消费者在乎的是足够小的空间占用——这个消费感知人人都有，但再往深想一步：所谓小，到底是薄还是直径小？日本消费者缺的是投影空间，所以你在乎的应该是直径小。所以我们把“mini”这个概念在日本打透了：基础款247直径的mini，往上还有298直径的“大号mini”。同样的产品到了别的国家，mini根本不是宣传重点，卖点是清洁性能；在日本，小直径就成了核心痛点。 欧洲也是一样。欧洲有比较多老房子、错层结构，所以Roomba Duo“把子机放到错层上”这个价值点是能讲通的。但如果未来中国全是精装大平层，你跟中国消费者讲错层，大家甚至不知道错层是什么。所以本地化一定是最关键的点——我们有很强的本地渠道、本地团队、本地理解，这是非常宝贵的资产。 硬氪：为什么继续用iRobot这个品牌？这个品牌有什么优势吗？ 李昊： iRobot本身是一个非常伟大的品牌，有很多未来的可能性，没有必要去做变更。首先它有非常忠实的用户基础和全世界范围的品牌认知；其次，说句可能反常识的话——Roomba这个词在消费者里的认知程度，其实比iRobot还高，在美国人们会说“我用的是Roomba”，不会说“我用的是iRobot”。 那为什么还要坚持iRobot这个品牌？你看过去有iPhone、iPad、iWatch，但未来，我认为这些“i”都不如iRobot。我们不会永远只focus在清洁赛道，iRobot这个名字本身有非常大的未来可能性，我们要做的是把这个品牌的价值巩固、完善，让消费者意识到它。 至于“低调”的问题，我觉得iRobot本身没那么低调，只是过去这些年因为运营模式显得低调了。现在我们要通过更好的产品、更好的信息传递，让大家认识到品牌的理念、价值观，以及我们真正以用户视角为中心的部分。 硬氪：中国的消费者这几年有什么新变化？ 李昊： 两个层面。第一是消费者认知在回归理性。中国扫地机市场全球占比非常大，但中国消费者对这个品类的了解偏晚、渗透率也偏低，前几年大家处于很宽容、很愿意尝鲜的状态，也为自己的尝试买了不少单。现在消费者对“清洁这件事本身”理解更透彻了，对自己需要什么样的产品开始清晰——过去大家把扫地机当尝鲜的东西，现在既要尝鲜，更要它能解决家里的问题。美国用户早就把扫地机当工具了，中国正在经历这个转变。 第二是家居环境的变化。中国装修从早期的没风格，到地中海、法式、新中式，再到现在非常明显的意式趋势。有个细节：现在精装房交付的地板基本都是浅灰偏哑光的，而拆地板是件很复杂的事，这个颜色基本决定了后面只能往意式走——新中式、法式、美式都不太合适了，意式好看又符合精装房交付标准，一定会成为主流趋势。而新意式现在是全球性的现象级趋势，美国的新家庭也往这个方向走。家具种类、桌椅沙发、布局都会随之变化，扫地机怎么契合这种环境，是我们该去研究的。 洗衣机、冰箱不是我们的方向 硬氪：叠加人形机器人、具身智能的想象，扫地机这个市场会不会发生我们没有看到的变化？ 李昊： 我个人观点是，完全具身进入家庭还需要时间。作为消费品，价格永远是关键要素，具身的成本还是比较贵的。但我非常看好这个方向的未来，它一定会往更多形态发展，不局限于纯扫地机，可能是“轮子+机械臂”的方式承载更多功能，像一个更高的家庭管家。中间阶段我更倾向于一个方向：基于扫地机这种移动底盘，加上3D传感器，再加上机械臂。 硬氪：很多中国企业每年都在扩品类，你们在品类上怎么规划？ 李昊： 两个方向。第一是清洁相关领域——扫地机、洗地机、吸尘器我们都会考虑，iRobot和在清洁层面深耕了很久，我们在北美已经发布了洗地机，今年接下来在中国也会发布。第二是机器人相关类目，iRobot在这个领域积累很深，展台下面你能看到我们不止做扫地，还有很多机器人技术的积累。我们会围绕清洁和机器人两个方向不断延伸。 但我们不会乱做，洗衣机也搞一个、冰箱也搞一个，那不是我们的方向。 硬氪：怎么克制这种诱惑？看到新品类、新机会，不做其实挺难的。 李昊： 任何一个行业，你光去看，无论红海与否，都能看到机会点。但要做还是不做，要回归理性判断。我们有一套评估模型，简单说就是“五看”：看宏观、看行业、看市场、看用户、看竞争，最后再看自己。这样每个行业你都能看到一个大概的ROI——所有行业都有ROI，但资源永远是有限的，你一定要聚焦。 同样2000个人的团队，我可以去做很多品类，但我更期望先用这2000个人聚焦做好几个品类，去解决那个核心问题——消费者买了两次之后不想再买的问题。改变行业，这是我们真正期待的事情。 硬氪：您自己是技术出身？ 李昊： 对，我是研发和产品背景出身，现在宏观都会管理，但更熟悉的还是产品和研发。不过我说的产品和研发视角不是工程师视角，而是从消费者出发的视角——早年我做纯产品研发的时候，就喜欢到各个国家跟经销商、零售商聊天，问他们的痛点和问题，再基于这些去规划产品。 技术卷到了平滑段，市场的活力还在 硬氪：今年在IFA逛下来，包括欧洲AI行业的发展，有什么让您印象深刻的？ 李昊： 从产品技术层面，我看了部分展馆，会感觉有点陷入僵局了——还是不断卷单一参数，逐渐走到技术曲线的平滑段，缺乏新意。所以我说我们今年还蛮不一样，都是从系统层面、消费者层面思考问题。 但从另一个视角看，市场的活力还在：人流在这里，大量产品需求、消费者需求、渠道需求都在。关键是各个品牌方怎么去满足这些需求。 硬氪：所以您对行业是中性还是乐观？ 李昊： 对行业我非常乐观。它正处在一个要往下一个渗透率阶段蓬勃发展的阶段——现在还是很低，全球平均渗透率，发达国家加上中国也就10%出头，空间是有的；产品成熟度也渐渐到了，开始出现真正有用的系统性解决方案。 市场角度我也乐观。这两天我见了非常多经销商、零售商，他们的需求很大，而且有大动作——比如单一国家的经销商，已经开始准备5000万欧元的大投入。 硬氪：经销商渠道的竞争现在也像产品和参数这么激烈吗？ 李昊： 挺激烈的，这源于行业变化。欧洲过去以线下渠道为主，是一个赢者通吃的模式——积累越深、关系越硬，就会持续变大。但现在渠道的多样性，包括线上渠道的可能性出现，给了很多新兴公司机会，无论是中国公司还是本土新公司。竞争在变激烈，渠道复杂度在变高，营销复杂度也在变高——从传统PR到现在大量红人的引入。但机会也更多：谁能更适应新的营销和市场规则，谁就能获得更多市场份额。 硬氪：现在展会上80%都是中国企业，卷到最后是中国企业卷中国企业，展会会不会越来越没意思？ 李昊： 还好。展会存在的意义，永远是服务当地的用户和当地的客户，参展商是谁并不改变这一点。目前中国公司势头比较强劲，所以中国公司更多；未来如果有其他国家崛起，也会有更多别国公司出现，参展商的竞争永远存在。 但展会本身很重要——比如这两天我会见很多经销商、零售商，这是一个非常好的机会去跟大家共识我们的产品：我们为用户创造什么价值、方向在哪里。我们的经销商伙伴都是合作十几二十年的老伙伴，大家一条心去共创一个品牌，价值就很大。 打破，再融合 硬氪：反过来问，这次焕新归来，最不希望外界记住的刻板印象是什么？ 李昊： 过去这些年，iRobot可能传递了一个相对保守的印象：追求稳定，喜欢把一个平台做稳定之后，连续几年都卖一样的平台。这个要改变。 iRobot其实有非常庞大的技术积累——3000多件专利。 iRobot展示其3000多项专利 核心问题是之前的思路偏保守：如果这个平台work，就一直让它work下去，有了新技术先储备着。现在我们认为，为了满足消费者的需求，应该把更多的创新真正应用到产品上，把储备的技术落地到消费者的真实场景里。我们不再是那个“平台能用就一直用”的公司，我们会更创新、更年轻。虽然我们有36年历史，但现在也是一家年轻的公司——昨天发布产品时，我们的节目表演都是rap的形式，就是想告诉大家：我们历史很悠久，但我们非常潮、非常年轻化、充满活力。 硬氪：这次借着IFA见了很多经销商，讲得最多的是什么？讲得最少的是什么？ 李昊： 讲得最多的是产品策略，但我不是去讲技术细节，而是讲我为什么开发这些产品、从用户心智出发是什么样的——因为最后营销和销售不只我们发力，经销商也要发力，他们是否理解、能否把信息传递给消费者，很关键。所以我要跟他们共识：这个产品怎么从消费者视角出发，真正的优势是什么。 高层级战略的事反而不怎么聊了——我1月份就开始管理，一直在到处跑，跟经销商都很熟，战略、合作关系这些1月份就聊过了。聊得最少的是商务商业的细节，或者要谈判的事情，因为大家都建立在绝对的互信和对品牌的热爱之上，都愿意多走一步。 硬氪：最后一个问题，您希望给iRobot的伙伴们讲些什么？ 李昊： 我希望跟大家说，所有人都把心态打开：所有我们认为不对的事、错误的事，都大胆提出来，把它解决掉，我们永远做正确的事。这是快速调转不正确方向的机会，我们要非常快地把过去觉得不对的事情都改掉，长此以往，iRobot会不断进化，同时带动清洁机器人行业往正确的路线前进。

items.title: Princess Diana's 'revenge dress' goes up for auction
items.summary: A dress worn by Princess Diana dubbed her "revenge dress" is being put up for auction. The late Princess of Wales wore the strapless black silk evening dress
items.text: A dress worn by Princess Diana dubbed her "revenge dress" is being put up for auction. The late Princess of Wales wore the strapless black silk evening dress to a party in London hours after her then-estranged husband Prince Charles admitted to committing adultery during their marriage. Her dramatic arrival at the Serpentine Gallery in 1994 in the outfit became an iconic pop-culture moment. Auction house Sotheby's expects the dress to sell for up to £220,000 ($300,000) when it goes under the hammer on 9 December - the first time it has been up for auction since 1997, when the princess sold 79 of her dresses just months before her death to raise money for charities. Morgane Halimi, Sotheby's global head of handbags and fashion, said in a statement that Princess Diana "understood instinctively" that fashion can be a language in its own right. "On her own terms, Princess Diana turned the dress into one of the most powerful messages she ever made, during one of the most scrutinised and emotionally charged episodes of her life," she said. "She walked into a moment in which so much of her story was being told for her and, through what she chose to wear, reclaimed the narrative for herself." The same evening as the Serpentine Gallery fundraising dinner, a documentary had aired in which the Prince of Wales (now King) had admitted that he had been unfaithful to Diana, after years of rumours and media reports. The content of the ITV interview had been leaked a few days prior, meaning Diana's first public appearance after it aired was widely interpreted as her reply. Anna Harvey, her stylist at the time, has been reported as saying that the princess "wanted to look a million dollars". She made a last-minute wardrobe change before heading out to the event, setting aside a less striking Valentino gown in favour of the off-the-shoulder dress with an asymmetric hemline and chiffon train by Greek designer Christina Stambolian, which she accessorised with a royal necklace, black clutch and black heels. The "revenge dress" will be toured around the world prior to its sale, appearing at Sotheby's London showroom from 18 to 24 September, before heading to Hong Kong for the start of October, Geneva for the start of November and then on to New York, where it will be sold. It was last auctioned by Diana herself, as one of dozens of items sold to raise funds for cancer and Aids charities. The dress was bought by then-Glasgow resident Briege Mackenzie and her husband Graeme, who paid £39,098 for it. She told the Independent , external at the time that they had purchased the item not to wear - "I can't fit in it," she said - but because the proceeds were going to charity Children First. Mackenzie said in a statement issued by Sotheby's on Thursday: "My late husband and I knew that this dress was something special. "Princess Diana was walking into the worst night of her life and you would never know it to look at her. It went from a cocktail dress to a statement in the time it took to photograph her. "Thirty years on, you can say the words anywhere in the world and everyone knows exactly which dress you mean." She added that she had decided to sell the dress following the death of her husband, with whom bidding on it had been "one of the great days of our life together". Sotheby's said that a rare copy of the 1997 auction catalogue, signed by Diana and Stambolian, and which credits Prince William for the idea to auction the dress, will be sold alongside it. Part of the proceeds from the sale will be donated to Royal Edinburgh Hospital via the NHS Lothian Charity. The vintage Jaguar XJ40 car that Diana had arrived at the Serpentine Gallery event in was sold at auction earlier this year for £66,250. The dress, however, is expected to fetch a considerably higher price - though it would not be the first time an item from the princess's wardrobe has sold for a significant sum. One of Diana's sweaters, featuring a black sheep among rows of white ones, was sold for £920,000 at an auction by Sotheby's in New York in 2023.
